newsitem.title: GERMANY: Banks to decide on buyback of some Telekom stock.
newsitem.headline: Banks to decide on buyback of some Telekom stock.

text.p: The three banks that coordinated the flotation of Deutsche Telekom AG will decide in coming days whether to exercise an option to buy back some of the shares, Dresdner Bank AG said.

The "greenshoe", or oversubscription option, enabled the banks coordinating last Monday's flotation -- Dresdner, Deutsche Bank AG and Goldman Sachs -- to issue 90 million shares on top of the basic volume of 600 million.
But the option also allows the banks to buy the additional shares back if the share price is perceived to have fallen too much.

The Telekom shares, with an issue price of 28.50 marks, rose as high as 34.10 marks on their first day of trade on Monday but have since fallen as low as 31.75 marks amid profit-taking. They were quoted at 31.85 marks at 1025 GMT in Frankfurt bourse trade on Thursday.
"It is normal for the price to fall in the first days," Hansgeorg Hofmann, management board member in charge of investment banking at Dresdner, told reporters at a dinner on Wednesday evening.
"The next days will be critical to see if the selling continues. In the coming days we will say how we will exercise the greenshoe option," Hofmann said.
Hofmann said the issue had been a success but added that he would have preferred to see Telekom shares start trade at 31.50 marks rather than opening higher and then falling.
The shares were still at a premium of five to 10 percent to the issue price, though, he noted.

Asked why the issue volume was topped up by 100 million shares to 600 million just one week before the flotation, Hofmann said that given overwhelming demand for the shares, their price would have "exploded" without the top-up, exposing Telekom to criticism that the issue price had been too low.
He also said there had been less speculative buying and selling in the Telekom shares than was the case with the flotation of British Telecom in the 1980s.
"If you compare it with British Telecom there has been less gambling and less of a price explosion," Hofmann said.

Asked if the coordinating banks gave their trading divisions free rein to buy and sell Telekom shares, Hofmann said, "If we undertake trading to stabilise the price for the syndicate, that would be totally separate from proprietary trading and from trading on behalf of customers business. There are Chinese Walls."
